Dose adjustments are necessary when co-administering lapatinib, as it increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, can elevate the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This effect may persist for up to 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Esterified estrogens may antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of liraglutide, reducing its efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Estrogens can impair glucose tolerance, potentially reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 6. Oral estrogens may reduce the serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to lonapegsomatropin, necessitating higher doses of lonapegsomatropin in patients receiving oral estrogen replacement therapy. 7. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Esterified estrogens increase the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Meropenem/vaborbactam may reduce the levels or effects of oral forms of esterified estrogens by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Mitotane decreases the levels of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. As a strong CYP3A4 inducer, mitotane may necessitate dosage adjustments for co-administered CYP3A4 substrates. Monitoring is essential. 13. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. If estrogens are used for contraception, there is a risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 24. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Siponimod and esterified estrogens both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution is advised during co-administration and in the weeks following therapy. Consider the half-life and mode of action of immunosuppressive drugs to avoid additive effects. 31. Oral estrogens may reduce the serum IGF-1 response to somapacitan, necessitating higher doses of somapacitan. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 32. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Stiripentol affects CYP1A2 metabolism and may require dosage adjustments for co-administered CYP1A2 substrates. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. As a weak CYP3A4 inducer, tecovirimat may necessitate monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 37. Teriflunomide decreases the levels of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may compromise the efficacy of estrogens used for contraception or hormone replacement therapy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Esterified estrogens decrease the levels or effects of valproic acid by increasing its elimination, potentially leading to increased seizure frequency. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 45. Esterified estrogens may decrease the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Estrogens may inhibit the hepatic metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, imipramine, nortriptyline), potentially increasing plasma concentrations and adverse effects. However, such interactions are uncommon. 47. Esterified estrogens decrease the levels of folic acid, L-methylfolate, and pyridoxine by altering their metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 48. Oral estrogens may shift magnesium from the blood to tissue storage, reducing serum magnesium levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 49. Esterified estrogens may reduce the effects of metyrapone, leading to subtherapeutic responses. It is generally advisable to discontinue estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration. 50. Mycophenolate may decrease the effects of esterified estrogens by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 51. Phytoestrogens may antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of esterified estrogens. The clinical significance is unknown. 52. Pleurisy root may theoretically reduce the effects of esterified estrogens by an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 53. Boron may increase the levels of esterified estrogens by altering their metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown.
